title: Symbol under the capture tape head
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $s$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. For any captured word $u$, optional administrative state $q$, natural number $i\le |x|$, integer offset $j$, and output word $o$, the symbol under the last work-tape head in the corresponding canonical pairing configuration is the content of the buffer tape for $u$ at $j$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine
replaced:
Let $M$ be a finite machine, $u$ a captured word, and $j \in \mathbb{Z}$. In every
canonical pairing configuration over $M$ with captured word $u$ and capture head
at offset $j$, the symbol under the last work head is the cell of the buffer tape
of $u$ at $j$, that is, the $j$-th bit of $u$ when $0 \le j < |u|$ and the blank
otherwise.
